entries.body: Beautiful day — we are dead downwind with full sails, lots of sunshine, it's great to be hot! Only problem is boat speed, down to 4 knots. More comfortable though, everyone is feeling better.
entries.conditions: Dead downwind, full sails, 4 knots. 24-hour run — 132 miles.

entries.body: Funny ocean — stirred up and wild one day, flat calm the next. The wind mostly fizzled out last night and we ended up motoring for 12 hours. Entered Minerva Reef at 2 pm. Fidelio and Amanetes were [there], got a bunch of wahoo.
entries.conditions: Wind: fizzled; motored 12 hours. Entered Minerva Reef at 2 pm.

entries.body: On our way again, weather report was good. Brian and I wanted to stay and walk on the exposed reef at low tide. North Minerva Reef was pretty weird, with no land at all. It was quite comfortable though behind the breaking reef. 20–25 today, SE winds, rather bumpy but getting smoother. Hope for this all the way, wouldn't be too bad!
entries.conditions: Short pause at North Minerva Reef (a submerged atoll, no land). Wind: SE, 20–25 knots.

entries.body: Well aren't we lucky! The wind let off and backed during the night, can you believe we are poled out again! We have been running the mizzen stay sail all day, it looks very nice. It's fun to fly it. Rolling some but otherwise it is comfortable. Sunny skies but it is not hot, air is cool. What are we getting into? The water is a beautiful blue, fish are flying, everyone is happy.
entries.conditions: Wind: eased and backed; poled out, mizzen staysail flying. 24-hour run — 133 miles.

entries.body: We never expected to be flying spinnakers on the way to New Zealand! Flew poled-out genoa, stay sail, main, and mizzen drifter all last night, did 5 knots, it was beautiful under a waxing moon. Wind started dying at sunrise, started motoring at 12:30. Will shut down the beast this evening to get some rest. At least it's hot and sunny today — we are enjoying that!
entries.conditions: Four sails flying overnight, 5 knots; then motoring as wind died. 24-hour run — 110 miles.

entries.body: What a beautiful day! The wind picked up at sunrise and we put up the stay sail and mizzen drifter, great sailing at 5 knots, lots of sunshine, we all enjoyed ourselves. Brian got into a map project. Charlotte doing very well on such light winds. We are reaching again, NW winds.
entries.conditions: Wind: NW, light; reaching at 5 knots. 24-hour run — 95 miles.

entries.body: Nothing lasts forever, and today is a different day. Wind turned NW last night, still light, then SW and was blowing 20–25 by sunrise. We are on our ear, can't quite hold the course, bashing along. Lots of fun! Oh well, knew we had to get nailed eventually! I saw the most perfect green flash last night!
entries.conditions: Wind: SW, 20–25 knots; hard on the wind. 24-hour run — 105 miles.

entries.body: It was rough trying to eat dinner last night, lentil soup was all I could manage. Then at 2 am we were motoring! Weather is so unpredictable here — changing every 12 hours or so. Been sailing all afternoon with a light west wind, turning NW, 2½ knots. It is pleasant at least! We won't complain, lots of sun, easy to cook.
entries.conditions: Wind: light west, turning NW, 2½ knots. 24-hour run — 119 miles.

entries.body: We saw a nice green flash last night — went along with the perfect cloudless sky at sunrise. Today is not so pretty — gray, [thin] clouds marching along, kind of breaking up as they pass over. Seems to be a stalled-out front, NW winds to 25 knots today. Charlotte is flying! 6–7 knots steady. We are reeling down the latitude, in the 30's now — brrr!
entries.conditions: Wind: NW to 25 knots; 6–7 knots steady. Into the 30s of latitude. 24-hour run — 117 miles.

entries.body: Oops — skipped a day. It was awful, motored into south winds. Still motoring today, at least we see land. Did not need head winds the last 2 days. Want to get this over with — landfall at sundown. Bye to adventure, hi to grim reality. Landfall wasn't so bad after all — the sun came out, the wind came up lightly from the east and we sailed! Lots of birds on the water, big ones with yellow heads, white and black. The hills are green, very rugged. Sailboats everywhere! Aka is in the marina! We met them on Lazy Lightning and cruised Trinidad & Venezuela. Ed and Fran. They have been here for 12 years.
entries.conditions: Wind: south head winds, then a light easterly for landfall. Arrived New Zealand (Opua, Bay of Islands) at sundown.

entries.body: Tore ourselves away from Opua — it was difficult, as more people we knew kept coming in. Oric Halcum anchored next to us and Ken loved eating the mussels off the mooring buoys! Leo on Moonlight arrived, Bob & Robin on Buster, Joyce & Jack on 2nd Tri, Allusion, and Tanil & Annette on Kelebec. And who else — Lazy Lightning of course! We rented a car and visited Dave & Sue and the kids — Brian went to school with Ben and attended a symphony orchestra presentation in Auckland. Worked on the boat — bought a new stove, put up insulation because we were freezing! It is colder than we had anticipated — downright miserable at times. And windy! But now we're underway to Gulf Harbour marina on Whangaparaoa Peninsula, where Dave & Sue live. It is not easy sailing! Yesterday had 20–30, doing 7 knots under reefed main alone. Spent the night in Oke Bay, left early this morning to round Cape Brett. Motorsailed all day with light head winds — the curse of NZ. Stopped in Tutukaka — warm pleasant afternoon, very little wind, warm our bones.
entries.conditions: About three weeks at Opua and the Bay of Islands. Departed south for Gulf Harbour via Cape Brett and Tutukaka. Wind: 20–30, then light head winds.

entries.body: Whew! A long windy day! Daysails are very strenuous. Left Tutukaka at 6 am, for the 55-mile haul to Kawau Island. Saw some huge dolphins — big ones 6–8 feet long. Saw whales yesterday. It's pretty sailing along NZ's east coast, but you can't really enjoy it, it's so cold. Very little habitation along the coast line. We had some good sailing at times, over 7 knots to windward for a while. We are in a tiny, protected harbor, only a few local boats moored. Happy that we were able to sail the whole way, and average 5 knots.
entries.conditions: 55-mile daysail, Tutukaka to Kawau Island. Sailed the whole way, averaging 5 knots; over 7 knots to windward at times.

entries.body: Peaceful night in North Cove. Off again in gray morning to Gulf Harbour Marina — 10 miles sail to tip of peninsula. We are on the dock now with the cold south wind blowing on the boat, not very comfortable. Brian is thrilled, I am not. Hope it pays off.
entries.conditions: 10-mile sail, North Cove to Gulf Harbour Marina (tip of Whangaparaoa Peninsula). Cold south wind.

entries.body: Sailing again — it feels good! We spent 6 weeks in Gulf Harbour, didn't like it too much. The hot showers & internet access was good, but we hated the public showers. I worked for Dave Mackay, doing a website and then spent 6 days polishing some motor yacht. No fun cruising boats in Gulf Harbour, no kids for Brian to play with. We spent an evening with the Mackays (Flying Cloud) once a week, Brian spent the night several times. Went into Auckland one night for dinner, saw all the America's Cup boats at the Viaduct. Rented DVD's, watched a lot of movies, saw 2nd Harry Potter & Lord of the Rings on the big screen. Once I was done with work, we moved to Murrays Bay where Trevor & Leslie, (father we met in Tonga), live with their 4 kids, Jacob, Julia, Jasmine, & Jeremy (Cox, 70 Gulf View Dr). They are a great family. We had Christmas dinner at their house, Jake & Julia spent a lot of time on our boat. They took us for the day to Anawhata Beach on the west side, just 30 minutes from Auckland. We had a wonderful day, took a long hike up a canyon to an old Maori dam where there was a ring set in the rock. We had to go bouldering, walking through shoulder-high grass, wading the stream, walking in the woods. The view from the sand dunes on the beach was spectacular. The sand was black, the surf was white. Now we are moving north, to find warmer weather perhaps? Tried to get to Great Barrier Island, but the wind turned NE, so now we are at Bon Accord harbor on Kawau. Lots of boats here.
entries.conditions: After 6 weeks at Gulf Harbour. Tried for Great Barrier Island; wind turned NE, so anchored at Bon Accord Harbour, Kawau Island.

entries.body: Kawau was ugly and crowded, didn't care for it there. Left this morning with a brisk east wind, but of course it didn't last. We are rolling along at a very slow pace. Otherwise it is a beautiful warm! sunny day. We will try to anchor at the entrance to Whangarei tonight.
entries.conditions: Brisk east wind early, then light. Heading for the entrance to Whangarei.

entries.body: We loved Urquharts Bay, spent 5 days there, hiking and windsurfing. Ocean Beach on the other side was beautiful and we hiked all over Bream Head. Had a nice New Year's Eve, made potato gnocchi and drank wine. Then we went up to Whangarei for a week. Ugly nasty dirty there but we got a lot accomplished — rebuilt the anchor winch, got an oil pressure gauge — finally! Left Monday, came back to Urquharts Bay. Today we sailed north to Whangamumu. Very rolly, Brian & Thomas are seasick, I am kind of green too. But we had a nice sail and Whangamumu harbor is very picturesque, surrounded by cliffs. The remains of an old whaling station are here. No town, no houses!
entries.conditions: Sailed north from Urquharts Bay toward Whangamumu. Very rolly.

entries.body: More great hiking at Whangamumu — we we[re] exhausted yesterday after hiking to some coves with a sandy beach. There were birds singing every morning, very nice. The water was clear. Now we are at Omakiwi Cove, no other boats here, a pretty stand of piney trees behind a sandy beach. Great view to the west of the Bay of Islands, boats moving around. We enjoyed a close-up view of Cape Brett as we rounded the point.
entries.conditions: Rounded Cape Brett to Omakiwi Cove, Bay of Islands.
